Jordan: hi all, Jordan here, first day! :wave: M1 MacBook Air. switched to fish earlier. trying to get asdf going (python/node/rust) + dotfiles bootstrap. asdf fails building python 3.10 with openssl-related configure errors. also ssh keys won't persist between restarts (ssh-agent not auto-loading), and the 1Password CLI is asking for SSO but I don't have the company vault yet. who do I ping for Okta/vpn/git access? any quick fish-specific tips?

Samir: welcome Jordan! quick wins: on Apple Silicon you usually need Homebrew OpenSSL libs in your env so python build finds them. I do this in fish: 
``` 
brew install openssl@3 readline sqlite3 xz zlib
# in fish (put in ~/.config/fish/config.fish or conf.d):
set -x LDFLAGS "-L"(brew --prefix openssl@3)"/lib"
set -x CPPFLAGS "-I"(brew --prefix openssl@3)"/include"
set -x PKG_CONFIG_PATH ""(brew --prefix openssl@3)"/lib/pkgconfig"
# then force configure opts when installing python via asdf:
env CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl=$(brew --prefix openssl@3)" asdf install python 3.10.12
```
That avoids hacking system openssl.

Samir: nodejs requires the plugin's GPG key import once: 
``` 
bash -c "$(curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs/master/bin/import-release-team-keyring)"
asdf plugin add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git
asdf install nodejs 18.20.0
```

Noor: for ssh-agent on macOS new releases, use the apple keychain integration which keeps keys across reboots: 
``` 
# add once
ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
# in fish startup (create ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ssh-agent.fish):
if not set -q SSH_AUTH_SOCK
  eval (ssh-agent -c) >/dev/null
  ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 >/dev/null 2>&1; or true
end
```
This keeps the agent available to new Terminal/VSCode windows. If you prefer not to touch keychain, you can keep a small conf.d script that starts ssh-agent on login.

Noor: also, after you get 1Password access, run `eval (op signin redwood --output=env)` in fish to populate env vars for the session. we store developer-only examples in the handbook; don't commit real creds — use `~/.redwood/env.local` and add it to .gitignore.

ITSupport: Jordan — send your manager's email and employee ID (or open a ticket at https://itsupport.redwood.internal/new). Request tags: onboarding, vpn, git-access. If you post here I can fast-track adding you to GitHub teams and Okta.

dev_onboard_bot: checklist for Jordan created: [ssh-key, add-to-1password, install-asdf-runtimes, clone-dotfiles, request-vpn, join-github-teams] (0/6).

Jordan: thanks — followed Samir's brew + CONFIGURE_OPTS approach and python built fine 389. imported nodejs keys and node installed. used ssh-add --apple-use-keychain and it persisted after a reboot 609.

Jordan: quick question: some services have devcontainers, some don't. should I prefer devcontainer or local Docker for dev?

Noor: default to devcontainer when available (consistent tooling + less local host variance). if you need native ARM things or fast iteration with local rust toolchain, use local Docker or native as needed. ping @Noor if a service's devcontainer is broken — we try to keep them green.

Samir: also FYI, when using VS Code Remote - Containers with fish, ensure your user shell is set to /opt/homebrew/bin/fish in the container/user settings so terminal shells pick up asdf.

Jordan: Okta invite request sent here. ITSupport responded and started the ticket. big thanks everyone — will shout if anything else pops up :heart:
